items.q: What does Glean say most AI product steps really are?
items.a: **Bounded decisions**, such as intent classification, expert routing, ranking and citation checks, **not generation problems**.

items.q: What was Glean doing wrong before?
items.a: Paying **full LLM cost and latency** for answers that are really **yes/no or pick-one-of-N**.

items.q: How did Jev compare with Llama on query classification?
items.a: It nearly **doubled base Llama quality** and reached about **90% of a fine-tuned Llama** with **no training**.

items.q: What did a decision model do for expert routing?
items.a: Higher precision at about **8x lower latency**, worth the extra infrastructure.

items.q: How did the suggestion ranker improve?
items.a: On time in **99.2%** of cases versus ~90%, with **zero invalid outputs**.
They let **thresholds be tuned per customer**, even by a **self-tuning system**.

items.q: Why did decision-model judges speed up development?
items.a: Citation checks were **consistent across runs**, so you **don't repeat experiments**.

items.q: What happened to the security classifier's recall?
items.a: It rose from **31.5% to 90.2%** and removed **per-tenant GPU hosting**.
**Can the output be listed in advance?** No: use an LLM. Yes: use a **decision model**.

items.q: When is fine-tuning a classifier still worth it?
items.a: Only when **labels are stable and volume is high**; changing taxonomies favour **editing a prompt**.

items.q: How does Glean roll out AI changes safely?
items.a: A **golden eval set**, a **multi-week internal soak**, then **A/B tests** with customers.
